why: Integration Hub expansion: CRM connectors reduce manual data handling and support client adoption.
outcome: A polled Salesforce → EP sync via SOQL on SystemModStamp is specified, with Connected App OAuth, External ID matching and daily API-limit awareness; push-back is Phase 2.

summary: Native Integration - Cvent (Event Management) — Phase 2: Push-Back
driverRationale: Cvent push-back makes the integration two-way, a more complete connector clients avoid re-keying data with.
what: Adds Phase 2 push-back for the Cvent integration, writing ExpoPlatform visitor and exhibitor updates, including profile pictures and logos, back to Cvent.
why: Two-way sync keeps client systems of record current without manual re-entry.
outcome: Independently toggleable visitor, exhibitor and image push-back subscriptions are specified, reusing Phase 1 auth and ID mapping, with image-loop prevention flagged as a risk.

summary: Native Integration - HubSpot (CRM) — Phase 2: Push-Back
driverRationale: HubSpot push-back makes the CRM integration two-way, the higher-value phase of the connector.
what: Adds Phase 2 push-back for the HubSpot integration, writing ExpoPlatform visitor and exhibitor updates back to HubSpot Contacts and Companies.
why: Two-way CRM sync keeps client data consistent across systems.
outcome: Toggleable push-back subscriptions with a dedicated outbound field mapping are specified, needing extra write scopes; image push-back is not possible on HubSpot.

summary: Native Integration - Salesforce (CRM) — Phase 2: Push-Back
driverRationale: Salesforce push-back makes the CRM integration two-way for clients whose system of record is Salesforce.
what: Adds Phase 2 push-back for the Salesforce integration, writing ExpoPlatform visitor and exhibitor updates back to Salesforce Contacts, Leads and Accounts.
why: Two-way CRM sync for clients whose system of record is Salesforce.
outcome: Toggleable push-back with its own outbound mapping is specified, sharing Phase 1 credentials and the daily API quota; image push-back is not applicable.

summary: Unify favouriting into FavouriteService with per-object-type handlers
driverRationale: Consolidates favouriting into one service to reduce duplication and future maintenance risk; a review follow-up.
what: Consolidates all favouriting into one FavouriteService with per-object-type handlers instead of controller switch statements.
why: Follow-up from the EP-53978 / PR #4431 review to reduce duplication and keep new favouriting logic in one place.
outcome: A single service with visitor, exhibitor, product, brand and session handlers is planned, with public writes migrating gradually and reads optionally consolidated.

summary: Bulk connection delete is not private-favourite-aware
driverRationale: Fixes bulk delete for opted-out users' private favourites, a mobile flow gap reported by DLG.
what: Bulk connection delete now also removes opted-out users' private favourites, so they can bulk-remove what they bulk-added.
why: Found in QA scope inventory of the EP-53978 private favourites work; the asymmetry broke the mobile bulk-remove flow.
outcome: Bulk delete is aligned with single-disconnect behaviour and removes the owner's private favourite rows; the fix is in testing.

summary: N+1 queries in V3 Sponsors list — exhibitor logo gate resolves per-sponsor at serialization
driverRationale: Removes an N+1 query regression in the V3 Sponsors list before it degrades performance.
what: Removes an N+1 query pattern in the V3 Sponsors list, where each sponsor's exhibitor logo setting was resolved separately at serialisation.
why: Performance regression introduced by EP-47975's exhibitor logo gating on the sponsor chain.
outcome: Logo gating is to be resolved once per page rather than per sponsor, keeping the same image output.

summary: [DS] Onboarding Spike: Round Tables codebase & architecture review
driverRationale: Onboards a second developer to Round Tables to remove bus-factor risk before three feature stories start.
what: Onboarding spike that brings a second developer up to speed on the Round Tables architecture ahead of three upcoming feature stories.
why: Necessary knowledge-transfer step before HV-137/HV-143/HV-139 can safely begin implementation.
outcome: A written architecture alignment (current design summary in the new developer's own words, proposed extension points for each of the three stories, and agreed risks/open questions), reviewed by the original developer.

summary: Enforce view-only / event scope for admin permissions (deny-by-default in AccessControl)
driverRationale: Makes admin permissions deny-by-default, closing a security gap where view-only admins had full access on other events.
what: Makes admin permissions deny-by-default so an admin set to view-only or no access on one event no longer gets full access on every other event.
why: Security finding split out of the EP-55010 admin lockout investigation; restricted admins could act on events they should not.
outcome: The fix to fetchAccessZone is scoped with explicit caution, as a naive deny-by-default could lock out many production admins across tenants.

summary: [BE] Global rate-limit for Utils::sendException with repeat counting
driverRationale: Global rate limit stops outages flooding the alert channel with duplicates that drown other alerts.
what: Adds a global rate limit with repeat counting to exception notifications, so an outage no longer floods the alert channel with identical messages.
why: Generalises the local AI-search rate limit from EP-47675 to the whole platform and removes that workaround.
outcome: A per-call-site signature with memcached marker and counter suppresses repeats for 300s, reports the repeat count next time and fails open if the cache is down.

summary: API V3 - [POST] /api/v3/products/{id}/media (Upload product media file)
driverRationale: Public API v3 product media upload completes the v3 product capability offered to integrators.
what: New Public API v3 endpoint lets integrators upload media files to a global product, completing the v3 product-media capability.
why: Closes a known gap in the ongoing Public API v3 endpoint migration, keeping the media capability consistent with the already-shipped image (EP-55240) and video (EP-55242) upload endpoints.
outcome: New POST /api/v3/products/{id}/media endpoint supporting up to 10 files per product, content-based format validation, a 5MB cap, PDF thumbnailing, and a standardized response envelope.

summary: API V3 - [DELETE] /api/v3/products/{id}/media/{mediaId} (Remove product media file)
driverRationale: Public API v3 media removal completes the product media CRUD pair for integrators.
what: New Public API v3 endpoint removes a product media file safely, only physically deleting it once no other owner still references it.
why: Required counterpart operation to make the new product-media API usable end to end.
outcome: New DELETE /api/v3/products/{id}/media/{mediaId} endpoint unlinks a media file from a product; the underlying file/row is physically deleted only when no other owner (exhibitor, schedule, message, etc.) still references it.

summary: [DS] Onboarding Spike: Data Protocol 2.0 pipeline scope & architecture review (Elmurod)
epic: Implementation of the Data collection pipeline
driverRationale: Onboarding spike gives a new engineer context on the Data Protocol 2.0 pipeline before hardening work, reducing delivery risk.
what: Onboarding spike bringing a new DS engineer up to speed on the Data Protocol 2.0 pipeline architecture before hardening and testing work begins.
why: Front-loads necessary context before the 10-item hardening roadmap (dead-letter store, reprocessing, ClickHouse migration tooling, Australia routing, observability, etc.) and in-flight dual-write tickets land.
outcome: A written summary of the pipeline architecture in the engineer's own words, reviewed by senior team members, plus documented open questions before the follow-on tickets start.

summary: Add isScheduled:boolean to session items in sessionsCalendarView response
driverRationale: Adds a scheduled flag so the session calendar can mark sessions in a user's agenda, completing the calendar view.
what: Adds an isScheduled flag to the session calendar API so the calendar UI can highlight sessions already in a user's personal agenda.
why: Direct frontend requirement to complete the calendar-view feature built under EP-54343.
outcome: Every session item in the day/week sessionsCalendarView response now carries an isScheduled boolean (always false for guests), with no other change to the response contract.

summary: [EP:dev] N+1 + PHP-8 null-deref in hosted-buyer agent displayName lookups
driverRationale: Fixes an N+1 and a null dereference that would hard-fatal hosted buyer pages after the PHP 8 migration.
what: Fixes an N+1 query and a null-dereference bug in hosted-buyer agent name lookups that would hard-fatal once the platform moves to PHP 8.
why: Flagged as a moderate-severity finding in an audit; must be fixed before the planned PHP 8.x migration to avoid a production outage.
outcome: Implementation hints proposed (batch-loading agent attributes once instead of per-agent, and null-guarding the read using the safe pattern already present elsewhere in the same controller); final implementation left to the developer.

summary: [TechDept] [EP:dev] N+1 in participant export getParticipantData — per-event 'SELECT title' query per account (N×M events queries)
driverRationale: Removes an N×M query pattern in participant export found in audit, preventing slow exports at scale.
what: Removes an N+1 in participant export, where a separate event-title query ran for every account and every event it was active in.
why: Performance defect found in audit (moderate severity) on the export hot loop.
outcome: Event titles are to be loaded once and reused across the export, including the moderator all-events branch, with unchanged output.

summary: Exhibitor Events Calendar View - Mobile
driverRationale: Mobile calendar view for Exhibitor Events closes a feature gap versus the Sessions calendar for attendees and exhibitors.
what: Adds a full calendar view (1-day/3-day grid, overlap handling, filters, search) to the mobile Exhibitor Events screen, matching the Sessions calendar experience.
why: Closes a feature gap versus the existing Sessions calendar view and the exhibitor-events-in-sessions-calendar work, neither of which touched the independent Exhibitor Events screen.
outcome: A full calendar view for Exhibitor Events on mobile: 1-day/3-day grid, week-glance strip, overlap handling with overflow bottom sheets, track quick-filters, in-calendar search, filters, a Today button, and a toggle back to List View, driven by a web-configured default-view setting.

summary: reduce dev-mode compilation graph: lazy-load heavy layout subtrees and enable webpack lazyCompilation
driverRationale: Lazy loading cuts 20 to 35 second dev compiles, saving engineering time on every page change.
what: Cuts portal-ui dev-mode page compile times by lazy-loading heavy layout subtrees and enabling webpack lazyCompilation.
why: Developer productivity: slow dev compiles waste engineering time on every page change.
outcome: Measured with lazyCompilation: profile 35s to 15.7s, news 20s to 10.6s, groups 21.5s to 3.7s, with per-page graphs down to 9.9k–12.3k modules.

summary: Add relevant logs to data import
driverRationale: Import result logs let admins see what was created or skipped and why, reducing support investigation of imports.
what: Each data import produces a result log, with a summary in Log Info and a downloadable per-row file showing what was created, updated or skipped and why.
why: Import transparency, so admins can trust and fix imports, especially where duplicates arise from fake email generation settings.
outcome: A summary with counts, status and fake-email state is logged, plus the uploaded file echoed back with Row, Action and Reason columns for re-upload.

summary: File size upload issue on data import
driverRationale: Processing large imports in one pass prevents broken records and duplicate accounts caused by manual file splitting.
what: Lets admins import one data file of any size and get one trustworthy result, instead of splitting large files by hand.
why: Data integrity during bulk onboarding ahead of events, when errors matter most.
outcome: Required behaviours are set: one upload is one job and re-running after an interruption never duplicates data; the processing design is left to the team.

summary: [BE-NonTM]Translation: please apply the missing system translations.
customersCsv: DLG Markets GmbH, Frankfurter Buchmesse GmbH
driverRationale: Urgent missing EN/DE notification translations for live Frankfurter Buchmesse and DLG events already used by exhibitors.
what: Adds missing and corrected EN/DE notification translations for Frankfurter Buchmesse and DLG PotatoEurope exhibitors on live events.
why: Urgent client need: the events were live and exhibitors were already using the platform.
outcome: Approval and time-change notification strings are to be added and corrected in EN and DE.

summary: Add MultiStandLocation component and migrate sponsors to ExhibitorCard
driverRationale: Readable multi-stand locations and full sponsor cards match the design system and stop duplicated location logic across apps.
what: Adds a MultiStandLocation component so multi-stand exhibitors display readably, and merges Sponsors onto ExhibitorCard so sponsor listings show location, tags and products.
why: Needed to match the Figma design-system pattern (one stand plus a "+N" counter) and stop duplicating/drifting location-building logic across every consumer app.
outcome: New MultiStandLocation component ships in expo-react-components; ExhibitorCard now builds its own location from exhibitor.halls; ISponsor is merged into IExhibitor so SponsorsPopup renders full ExhibitorCards; the old SponsorCard is deprecated but not deleted, pending consumer migration.

summary: Spike: EDA on historical user interaction data for Recommender scoring enhancement
driverRationale: Analysis-only spike checks whether interaction data is dense enough before committing effort to a recommender approach.
what: EDA on historical like/favourite data to determine whether it's dense enough to build and evaluate a smarter, interaction-aware session recommender.
why: Needed hard evidence before committing engineering effort to either the category-weight or embedding-similarity scoring approach still on the table.
outcome: An EDA write-up covering historical interaction volume/density (an updated sparsity verdict versus the 2023 LightFM baseline), exposure-bias/impression-data findings, and a recommendation on offline vs. online evaluation strategy for the two remaining candidate approaches.

summary: Move account creation earlier in Registration flow (prerequisite for cart approach) - ON HOLD
epic: On Hold Registration Stories and Post Registration work
driverRationale: Creating the account before payment is a prerequisite for the cart payment approach in the new registration and payment work.
what: Creates the registrant's account before payment starts rather than after submission, as a prerequisite for the cart payment approach (on hold).
why: Blocks the cart/basket payment approach in EP-55566, which needs a reserved account before payment.
outcome: Draft criteria move account creation ahead of payment, update ordering tests and audit dependent code; the story is on hold.

summary: Handle VAT charged when VAT-number check service is unavailable at checkout - ON HOLD
epic: On Hold Registration Stories and Post Registration work
driverRationale: Handles VAT when the check service is down, avoiding incorrect invoices and manual refunds to exempt B2B customers.
what: Defines how checkout should handle VAT when the VAT-number check service is down, instead of silently overcharging exempt business customers (on hold).
why: Invoice correctness and tax compliance; overcharged customers need formal invoice corrections.
outcome: Options to block checkout, charge and auto-correct with a refund and credit note, or retry are set out for a product and engineering decision; on hold.

summary: Enhancing Exhibitor Import to Attach Brands Across Events
customersCsv: DLG Markets GmbH, ANWR Group eG
driverRationale: Import now carries exhibitor brands across events so they need not be recreated each edition; raised by ANWR and DLG.
what: Exhibitor import and adding exhibitors from the global database now attach their existing brands, and brand–product links, to the new event.
why: Brands are long-term assets used in sponsorship and search, but exhibitors had to recreate them for every event edition.
outcome: Recurring events carry exhibitors' brands over automatically, with no new import column and no duplicate brands.

summary: Region filters
driverRationale: Optional region subfilter lets organisers who collect region let visitors narrow listings within a country.
what: An optional Regions subfilter under Country for exhibitor, product, brand, pavilion, delegate, speaker and buyer listings on web.
why: Some organisers collect region at registration and want visitors to narrow results within a country.
outcome: Visitors expand a country to pick regions, like category subfilters; it's off by default and web only.

summary: [TechDept] [EP:dev] PaymentInvoiceService: tolerate null ambient lang when generating invoices (TypeError hardening)
driverRationale: Hardens invoice generation against a null language that could return a 500 after a successful payment.
what: Hardens invoice generation so a null ambient language no longer throws a TypeError that could return a 500 after a payment has already succeeded.
why: Tech debt agreed in the PR #4578 review: the hazard is real though rare, and would give clients a 500 for a recorded success.
outcome: Invoice generation is to tolerate a null language across the four no-language call sites, closing the TypeError path.

summary: [Tech debt] - Chosen [Anchor option] is not updated after element [Anchor] rename
driverRationale: Keeps site builder anchor links in sync after rename so organisers' on-page navigation does not break.
what: Keeps the chosen anchor option on linked buttons and links in sync when the anchor element is renamed in the site builder.
why: Frontend tech debt; stale anchor links break on-page navigation that organisers have set up.
outcome: Renaming an anchor is to update the anchor option selected on linked clickable elements.

summary: Community-as-home-page redirect drops query params and URL fragment
driverRationale: Keeps query params and fragment on the community-as-home redirect so sign-in and reset-password deep links work again.
what: Makes the community-as-home-page redirect keep query parameters, the URL fragment and the locale, so links such as /#signIn still work.
why: Frontend routing tech debt: deep links like the sign-in modal were silently broken on community-as-home sites.
outcome: The redirect target is to carry query, fragment and locale through, avoiding the lossy client-side hop.

summary: Global search. UI improvements based on feedback from IMEX
driverRationale: Global Search page refinements from IMEX feedback on the newly launched search page.
customerEvidence: summary: 'Global search. UI improvements based on feedback from IMEX'
what: Global Search results page refinements: a fixed search field under the banner, counts on Show all buttons, a bold results title, even News cards.
why: User feedback after the new search page launched asked for a more streamlined page.
outcome: The results page is cleaner, counts match their sections, and sponsored blocks are renamed Sponsored Exhibitors and Sponsored Products.

summary: [BE] Onboarding into Ticketing functionality + study new code architecture (PR #4510) for future refactoring
driverRationale: Onboarding research builds Ticketing and new-architecture fluency ahead of a refactor of weak monolith code.
what: Onboarding/research task building developer fluency in Ticketing and a proposed new architecture (PR #4510) ahead of a planned Ticketing refactor.
why: Prerequisite knowledge-building step for a planned future Ticketing refactor.
outcome: Developer understanding of Ticketing end-to-end and the new architecture pattern from PR #4510, plus a documented list of candidate refactor areas; no code changes.

summary: IconModal: paddings and title typography do not match the Design System
driverRationale: Fixes IconModal spacing at the root to match the design system, removing local style patches across about 41 call sites.
what: Fixes IconModal's padding, gaps and title typography to match the Figma design system exactly, removing per-consumer style patches across ~41 call sites.
why: Design-system-fidelity issue surfaced by comparing the shipped component against its Figma spec node; the current "correct" spacing only worked by coincidence, not by design.
outcome: Reworked slot styles (uniform 24px padding, single 32px gap, correct 18px/1.2 bold title, 8px radius plus border, 424px default width), full Storybook coverage of slot combinations, and removal of local sx/width workarounds in admin-ui.

summary: [TechDept] profile products: guard add/edit form against direct ?add URL access
driverRationale: Guards the product form against direct URL access so restricted users cannot bypass configured product limits.
what: Closes a bypass where direct URL navigation let restricted users open the add/edit product form even when the UI correctly hid the button.
why: Security/business-logic gap discovered in review; needed to prevent users from exceeding configured product limits or editing restrictions via URL manipulation.
outcome: Routing decisions now use the same single "can add/can edit" gate as the button; unauthorized direct navigation redirects to the product list instead of rendering the form, with backend enforcement also to be verified.

summary: Migrate Statistic Events from WebSocket to HTTP ingest gateway
driverRationale: Moves statistic events to the DS HTTP ingest gateway because some events never arrived over the WebSocket path.
what: Moves browser statistic events off the shared WebSocket to the data science team's HTTP ingest gateway, which validates and forwards them to S3 and ClickHouse.
why: The data science team is replacing the path, taking our backend out of the analytics flow.
outcome: The three analytics WS actions (statistics, online dwell, notification clicks) are to post to the ingest gateway; chat, presence and push stay on WebSocket.

summary: [Spike] Research the steps needed to change the search engine to AI Search
driverRationale: Spike scopes switching Exhibitors search to AI Search, work raised by IMEX, so it can be estimated and planned.
what: Scoping spike estimating the effort, risks and infrastructure needed to migrate the Exhibitors search engine to AI Search.
why: Needed so the team can estimate EP-55996 confidently and the EM can plan the work into a sprint.
outcome: A technical brief (target state, gap analysis, risks/open questions, phased plan with T-shirt estimates) published and linked to EP-55996.

summary: [Invoice&Payments] Add Account ID / ID as a search parameter on Transaction Dashboard and Invoice Payments pages
driverRationale: Direct client request from ACI to search transactions by Account ID to cross-check against Stripe.
what: Extends Transaction Dashboard and Invoice Payments search to match Account ID, so client ACI Asia-Pacific & Middle East can cross-check transactions against Stripe quickly.
why: Direct client request and follow-on from the earlier search feature (EP-54690), confirmed feasible by engineering.
outcome: The existing search field/button on both pages now also matches (partial) Account ID / ID, with the same trigger, reset and empty-state behavior as the original name/email search.

summary: Enforce per-event access scope for configured admins (deny-by-default in AccessControl)
driverRationale: Deny-by-default admin scope stops view-only restrictions being bypassed on other events, a security and trust issue.
what: Admins restricted on one event stay restricted on every event they have not been explicitly granted, instead of falling back to the default access template.
why: Organisers expect per-event restrictions to hold; the bypass is a security and trust issue.
outcome: A new resolution order is defined: explicit row wins, any configured admin is denied elsewhere, and only never-configured admins use DEFAULT SETTINGS.

summary: Post Code Field Validation for Registration Forms
driverRationale: Post code validation on registration forms; only the title describes the change.
what: Adds validation for the post code field on registration forms (details are in a linked Confluence page only).
why: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
outcome: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumed to validate post codes entered in registration forms.

summary: All 404s return HTTP 200 — soft-404 caused by the next-i18n-router rewrite
driverRationale: Returns real 404s instead of soft-404s so junk paths are not indexed and monitoring can detect broken routes.
what: Makes non-existent pages return a real HTTP 404 instead of 200, fixing soft-404s caused by the next-i18n-router rewrite.
why: SEO and monitoring: junk paths were indexable and uptime checks could not tell broken routes from healthy ones.
outcome: The status loss is to be pinned down in the rewrite path and fixed so notFound() yields a 404 across the app, including site-builder slugs.

summary: [Tech] Product uploads: move storage I/O out of the DB transaction; lock the product row against concurrent lost updates
driverRationale: Moves upload I/O out of the DB transaction and locks the product row, preventing lost updates, orphaned files and connection exhaustion.
what: Fixes product upload endpoints so slow file I/O no longer blocks the DB transaction and concurrent uploads can no longer silently overwrite each other's result.
why: Correctness and scalability defect discovered in the product upload path; needed before it causes data loss or connection exhaustion at scale.
outcome: Uploads now validate and store the file first with no open transaction, then link it in a short transaction with permission/limit checks re-run; failed links auto-clean the stored file; concurrent writes to the same product now queue via row locking instead of silently overwriting; ~30 new unit tests, API contract unchanged.

summary: Cache-Control: public is applied to every route regardless of auth or cookies
driverRationale: Stops cookie-dependent pages being marked publicly cacheable, preventing one visitor's page being served to another via the CDN.
what: Fixes a caching bug where cookie-dependent/signed-in pages were marked publicly cacheable, risking one visitor's personalized page being served to another.
why: DevOps enabled CDN caching for custom domains and asked the frontend team to confirm cookie-dependent pages weren't marked public before extending caching further.
outcome: Routes split into anonymous (kept public/cacheable) vs personal (private, no-store) groups; Vary: Cookie added where relevant; audited that no public response carries Set-Cookie; a route/header matrix handed to DevOps.

summary: [TechDebt] Global Search: remaining backend refactoring from code review
driverRationale: Clears deferred Global Search code-review findings, hardening config, access checks and error handling.
what: Addresses remaining Global Search backend code-review findings: constructor-based config, policy-layer access checks, and hardened error handling.
why: Agreed follow-up from the EP-47675 Global Search code review.
outcome: Constructor-based configuration, access rule moved into a policy, hardened typing and exception handling, followed by a review/QA pass.

summary: Utils::addToQueue reports its own SQS failure through itself — exponential retry loop that OOMs the process
driverRationale: Breaks a self-reporting retry loop that could run processes out of memory during any SQS outage.
what: Stops Utils::addToQueue reporting its own SQS failures through itself, which created a growing retry loop that ran the process out of memory.
why: A generic reliability defect found during testing of EP-53978; any SQS outage or credential issue could crash processes.
outcome: The failure path is to be decoupled from the queue it reports on, so an SQS failure is logged once rather than looping to OOM.

summary: Re-check which interaction events reach ClickHouse for an opted-out actor, and decide per action
driverRationale: GDPR audit of which interaction events reach ClickHouse for opted-out users, deciding suppression per action.
what: Audits which interaction events still reach ClickHouse for users who opted out of networking, and decides per action whether to suppress them.
why: Privacy and GDPR: decide the remaining ~40 action codes deliberately rather than defect by defect.
outcome: A per-action table over AnalyticsActionEnum is to record emit channel, whether it identifies the actor and the decision to keep or suppress.

summary: [TechDept] [adminUI] Sentry: tag events with tenant and user identity
driverRationale: Tagging adminUI Sentry events with tenant and user lets support and engineering find errors by customer faster.
what: Tags adminUI Sentry events with tenant, event and user identity so errors can be found by customer.
why: Observability: support and engineering need to search errors by customer.
outcome: After auth, setUser plus ep.tenant and ep.event_id tags are to be set and cleared on logout, using indexed tags rather than contexts.

summary: [portalUI] Sentry: tag events with tenant and user identity
driverRationale: Tagging portalUI Sentry events with tenant and user identity makes errors traceable to a customer, speeding diagnosis.
what: Tags portalUI Sentry events with tenant, event and user identity so errors can be found by customer.
why: Observability, aligned with the adminUI sibling ticket so one search works across both projects.
outcome: After auth, setUser plus ep.tenant and ep.event_id tags are to be set and cleared on logout, using the same tag names as adminUI.

summary: [TechDept] [adminUI] Sentry: upload source maps so production stack traces are readable
driverRationale: Uploading adminUI source maps makes production stack traces readable, cutting diagnosis effort.
what: Uploads adminUI source maps to Sentry so production stack traces show real functions and lines instead of minified bundle positions.
why: Observability: readable traces are needed to diagnose production errors.
outcome: Hidden source maps are to be generated, uploaded via @sentry/vite-plugin with a secured CI token, deleted locally, and matched to the runtime release.

summary: [portalUI] Sentry: confirm source map upload is not silently skipped in CI
driverRationale: Confirms portalUI source map uploads are not silently skipped in CI, so traces are readable when needed.
what: Confirms portalUI source map uploads to Sentry actually run in CI rather than being silently skipped when the auth token is missing.
why: Observability: silently minified traces are only discovered when someone needs them.
outcome: The token is to be checked or added as a secured pipeline variable, with an option to fail the production build when it is missing.

summary: [portalUI] Sentry: Report a problem action that flushes the replay buffer
driverRationale: Report-a-problem action attaches the real session replay to user reports, cutting effort spent reproducing non-throwing bugs.
what: Adds a portalUI "Report a problem" action that flushes the Sentry replay buffer and sends users to intake with the feedback event id.
why: Turns prose bug reports into reports with the actual session, breadcrumbs and network calls attached.
outcome: The action is to flush replay, call captureFeedback and pass the event id to intake, using the same URL parameter as adminUI and no SDK upgrade.

summary: [TechDept] [adminUI] Sentry: Report a problem action that flushes the replay buffer
driverRationale: Admin report-a-problem action gives support real session evidence instead of unreproducible prose reports.
what: Adds an adminUI "Report a problem" action that flushes the Sentry replay buffer and sends users to intake with the feedback event id.
why: Gives support the real session evidence for reported problems and makes use of the replay buffer already kept.
outcome: The action is to await replay flush, call captureFeedback and pass the event id to intake on the current @sentry/react v10 SDK.

summary: [adminUI] Sentry: Report a problem action that flushes the replay buffer
driverRationale: Duplicate of the adminUI report-a-problem ticket; gives support session evidence for non-throwing bugs.
what: Adds an adminUI "Report a problem" action that flushes the Sentry replay buffer and sends users to intake with the feedback event id (duplicate of the TechDept ticket).
why: Gives support the real session evidence for reported problems and makes use of the replay buffer already kept.
outcome: The action is to await replay flush, call captureFeedback and pass the event id to intake on the current @sentry/react v10 SDK.

summary: Meeting report extension. Subject and Message
driverRationale: Adds Subject and Message columns to the meetings report; only the title describes the change.
what: Extends the meetings report with Subject and Message columns (detail is in a linked Confluence page only).
why: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
outcome: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumed to add Subject and Message columns to the meetings report.

summary: Decide the source of truth for favourite counters: keep ClickHouse-only (accept the gap) or emit favourites server-side
driverRationale: Decides the source of truth for favourite counters to resolve under- and double-counting behind three parked defects.
what: Decides the source of truth for profile favourite counters: keep ClickHouse and accept the gap, or emit favourites server-side.
why: Three parked defects (EP-55702, EP-55697, EP-55707) share this root cause and cannot be fixed until the decision is made.

summary: ExpoIntelligence — requirements analysis & data-presence audit

summary: US-1: Access via unique email link (v1)
driverRationale: Tokenised email access is the foundation of the new ExpoIntelligence exhibitor insights portal.
what: Exhibitors can open the ExpoIntelligence insights portal from a tokenised email link without an ExpoPlatform login.
why: Foundation for the Exhibitor Insights Portal, delivered through email campaigns.
outcome: A token scoped to one exhibitor and event with expiry, revocation and read-only access is specified; delivery and revocation ownership are still undefined.

summary: US-2: Solo exhibitor view
driverRationale: Solo exhibitor view is the core use case of the new ExpoIntelligence insights portal.
what: A solo exhibitor lands directly on their own guided journey and full insights report in the ExpoIntelligence portal.
why: Core use case of the Exhibitor Insights Portal.
outcome: All 7 sections are to populate from live data scoped to the exhibitor, with no stand switcher; sizing awaits metric definitions and spike EP-56324.

summary: US-3: Stand summary (parent + children)
driverRationale: Stand summary aggregates parent and child exhibitor KPIs in the new insights portal.
what: Parent exhibitors see a Stand Summary aggregating their own and all child exhibitors' KPIs in the insights portal.
why: Exhibitors with sub-exhibitors need a stand-level picture.
outcome: Summed and deduplicated KPIs with a combined benchmark are specified; blocked on the dedup rule for buyers who met several children.

summary: US-4: Child switcher
driverRationale: Child switcher completes the parent and child experience in the new ExpoIntelligence portal.
what: Parent exhibitors can switch from the Stand Summary into any individual child exhibitor's insights report.
why: Part of the Exhibitor Insights Portal parent/child experience.
outcome: A switcher listing parent and children is specified, with one-click return and children unable to see siblings; depends on US-3.

summary: US-5: White-label branding
driverRationale: White-label branding makes the insights portal look like the organiser's own product to its exhibitors.
what: The insights portal carries the event's own logo on the gate, report header and exports, falling back to the ExpoPlatform mark.
why: The portal should look like the organiser's product to its exhibitors.
outcome: The event logo is to be pulled from Admin → General → Logo via the Event API; flagged as the lowest-risk story for early pickup.

summary: US-6: Guided journey + one-page report
driverRationale: Guided journey and one-page report with export deliver the approved ExpoIntelligence prototype as a product.
what: Builds the insights portal's guided journey and one-page report, with 12 insight cards over 7 sections and Excel/PDF export.
why: Deliver parity with the approved ExpoIntelligence prototype.
outcome: Every number is to trace to a defined metric query and exports include all unlocked sections; blocked on ~40 metric definitions.

summary: US-7: Benchmarks vs similar exhibitors
driverRationale: Peer benchmarks give exhibitors context in the new ExpoIntelligence insights portal.
what: Shows exhibitors their percentile position against an anonymised peer cohort from the same event.
why: Benchmarks give exhibitors context for their event performance.
outcome: Cohorts of at least 8 with non-identifiable peers are specified; blocked on Legal anonymity sign-off and an undefined cohort definition.

summary: US-8: Buyer interaction insights
driverRationale: Buyer interaction insights are a core value of the new Exhibitor Insights Portal.
what: Shows exhibitors which buyers viewed, favourited, searched, messaged or met them, with profile context.
why: Buyer insight is a core value of the Exhibitor Insights Portal.
outcome: Listing only interacting buyers within lead-sharing rules is specified; blocked on undefined lead-sharing rules and buyer interaction coverage gaps.

summary: US-9: LLM coaching narrative
driverRationale: LLM coaching narrative is a later-phase premium layer of ExpoIntelligence, deferred until dashboards are validated commercially.
what: Adds an LLM coaching layer to the insights portal that writes plain-English narrative and a prioritised action plan per section, never inventing numbers.
why: Part of the ExpoIntelligence vision, but deliberately deferred until the dashboards are validated commercially.
outcome: Deterministic numbers with LLM-written narrative, cached per exhibitor and data version, are specified; low priority per the 7 Aug team decision.

summary: US-10: Paywall on dashboard (nice-to-have)
driverRationale: Paywall lets exhibitors self-purchase the full insights report, stated as a potential revenue stream.
what: Lets exhibitors self-purchase the full insights report from a paywalled preview on their dashboard (nice-to-have, v2).
why: A potential revenue stream for ExpoIntelligence, deferred behind v1 email-link access.
outcome: A locked preview, purchase unlock and auditable entitlement are specified; not to be sized until v1 ships and a payment decision lands.

summary: Bulk respond: remove full-team prefetch and pre-Apply sweep in favor of a post-apply grid refetch
driverRationale: Removes a slow prefetch that delayed Bulk Respond for large exhibitor teams, and a data-correctness risk in the patch logic.

why: The prefetch (and a second hidden sweep) existed only to support an optimistic client-side patch; removing them entirely, rather than swapping the data source, eliminated both the delay and a data-correctness risk in the patch logic.

summary: Media module: migrate Contract signatures from SharedKernel VOs to primitives

why: New-monolith architecture convention adopted in EP-52842; the Media module predated it and needed to catch up, the same as Categories/Locations/Exhibition already had.
outcome: Media module Contract signatures now use primitives (int, int[], ?int); VO translation moved into facade implementations; consuming code (mainly the Product module) updated accordingly.

summary: Add FBM Gabarito to remaining pages [Android]

what: Rolled out the FBM app's Gabarito typography to all remaining Android screens (~1010 elements across 451 layouts) for one consistent look end to end.
why: Client/brand-consistency requirement for the FBM app; a PO note flagging residual visual risk indicates this shipped ahead of an event under time pressure.

summary: Native Integration: Infosalon Exhibitor Push + SSO

what: Adds a native InfoSalons integration that pushes ExpoPlatform exhibitor data to the InfoSalons Exhibitor Portal and supports SSO login.
why: Extends the Integration Hub, following the Aditus exhibitor push pattern (EP-46657).
outcome: An ongoing outbound sync on create and update with API-key auth, plus JWT-signed SSO login and account sync endpoints, is specified.

summary: Banner sizing: single source of truth instead of hand-maintained per-page aspect-ratio constants
customersCsv: Frankfurter Buchmesse GmbH, Mercator Media Limited

summary: Return Button to Global search result page
driverRationale: Back-to-results path keeps attendees' Global Search context; part of Search Anatomy work raised by IMEX.

why: Direct UX gap in the unified Global Search experience, part of the broader Search Anatomy initiative.
outcome: A "Back to search results" path now appears on detail pages reached via Global Search (restoring the query), consistently across all result types, and is absent when the detail page was reached any other way.

summary: [TechDept][TM-dev/BE] Monolith: implement ICU MessageFormat rendering in the translation layer (plural/select)

what: Extends the unsaved-changes guard to the other iframe-embedded admin pages, so parent-frame navigation no longer silently drops edits.
why: The same data-loss bug EP-56400 fixed remained reproducible elsewhere in the admin.
outcome: The reusable guard is to be wired into the remaining embedded pages, replacing each page's own partial navigation warning.

summary: Internal admin panel search
driverRationale: Admin Panel search lets admins jump to settings instead of hunting through a panel too large to navigate.

driverRationale: Resets leaked static config between Codeception tests so full-suite runs stop producing false failures.

summary: [BE Test fail] Import suites are red — 53 failures across api-admin and cli, and nothing anywhere turns red

summary: Banners sizes streamline

summary: fix Avatar size="xxs" regression in TagSelect breaking build:types

summary: Move sitemap.xml generation to the frontend and make it locale-aware

summary: Restrict meetings for exhibitors without team members (rework)
